title: FW Lite design language: round 2
question: Three hybrids of The Exercise Book and The Thumb Index. Each gives the list/detail split a strong divider and groups the editor so your eye can follow it.

options.label: Bound Notebook
options.lineage: an exercise book lying open: list on the left page, entry on the right, the cover showing at the spine
options.thesis: List and entry are two pages bound by a spine in the cover colour; the editor keeps the red margin but drops full-page ruling.
materials: cover-colour spine between list and entry
ruled line only under each value
options.viewport: Green cover frames both pages; a dark spine separates them. Field groups (Word, Gloss, Definition) carry bold names; each meaning opens with a tinted band and a large red numeral in the margin.
options.risk: The green cover around everything is a strong commitment; the margin rule must not read as an error colour.

options.label: Tabbed Notebook
options.lineage: a thumb-indexed notebook: the letter tabs run down the page edge
options.thesis: The thumb-index strip IS the divider: a dark column of letter tabs between list and entry, the current letter lit in oxblood.
materials: field name column + values with an oxblood left rule
options.viewport: List grouped under letter headings in dictionary notation; the tab strip divides it from the entry; the editor is a two-column form: field name on the left, its writing-system values stacked on the right.
options.risk: The tab strip needs the project's own alphabet (from collation) to be honest; it takes 40px of width on desktop.

options.label: Printed Page
options.lineage: a printed dictionary page, with the editor set as a typeset table
options.thesis: A double rule divides list from entry like a page's column rule; the editor is a table whose field groups alternate a faint band so each row is easy to follow.
options.viewport: Charcoal shell; the list on a warm tint with an A–Z index inside its edge; a double rule; the entry as a table: field name, writing system, value, banded per field.
options.risk: The table reads denser than today's form; on phones the field-name column has to collapse above its values.
